Subject: Throughput tiers + trial credits for personalization inference

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo last week. Nimbus is planning a phased rollout of personalization and recommendations that will peak at high token volumes during flash sales. Before we unblock procurement, can you send a clear hosted rate card and an example slab for sustained throughput? Specifically:

- Baseline hosted API per-1M-token price (standard low-latency model)
- Discount breakpoints for monthly commit (e.g., 1B / 5B / 10B tokens) and sample math
- How burst credits / overage work vs reserved sustained throughput
- Any trial or sandbox credits you offer for integration and load testing

We can share expected qps distribution and token length after you confirm the right contact to receive the rate card. I attached Nimbus's security questionnaire for your CS/security team to review (see procurement CC).

Cheers,
Claire
Claire Nguyen
Head of ML Infrastructure, Nimbus Retail
claire@nimbusretail.com

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput tiers + trial credits for personalization inference

Claire —

Appreciate the detail and the security questionnaire. Attaching a concise rate card and an example throughput table for a few commit sizes (ratecard_v2.pdf, SLA_table.csv). Quick highlights inline to save time: 

- Baseline (hosted low-latency model): $12.50 per 1M tokens (pay-as-you-go).
- Committed tiers (monthly, sustained): 1B @ 30% off baseline; 5B @ 45% off; 10B+ @ 60% off.
- Burstable credits: customers can buy a pool of burst credits or configure a 10–20% burst buffer on top of sustained commit for short spikes; bursts are consumed before overage pricing applies.
- Overage: uncommitted tokens billed at baseline + step premium (variable by month).
- Pilot credits: we typically offer sandbox credits for integration and load-testing; proposing a $20k pilot credit that can be applied to hosted usage for 30 days while we validate traffic patterns.

To give sensible pricing for Nimbus we need two things: expected steady-state qps and typical sequence length distribution (90th/95th percentile). If you can share a 1-week sample (anonymized) or the requested_sample_traffic.csv we can run a quick simulation.

I'm happy to run through the slab math with your procurement team — if it helps, we can offer a short call later this week to walk through the SLA and credit terms.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales - Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
Attachments: ratecard_v2.pdf; SLA_table.csv

Subject: Re: Throughput tiers + trial credits for personalization inference

Claire, Vivek —

Adding some practical examples so procurement gets a quick read:

Example A (mid): 1B tokens / month committed
- Effective price: baseline $12.50 * (1 - 0.30) = $8.75 per 1M tokens
- Monthly cost approx: $8.75 * 1000 = $8,750

Example B (high): 10B tokens / month committed
- Effective price: baseline $12.50 * (1 - 0.60) = $5.00 per 1M tokens
- Monthly cost approx: $5.00 * 10,000 = $50,000

Notes: sustained commits assume even distribution; if your traffic is spiky (flash sales) you can pair a smaller sustained commit with burst credits — cheaper than overage in most cases. For long-term contracts (12+ months) we can re-surface an additional volume rebate tied to usage thresholds and a single-term ramp schedule.

If Nimbus plans to run a 30–60 day validation load, proposing the $20k pilot credit + an additional sandbox throughput allocation (equivalent to 500M tokens for load testing) — this avoids hitting overage while we're calibrating.

Happy to convert any of this into a clean procurement sheet — Vivek, want me to draft a one-page quote that procurement can sign?

—Ben
Ben Carter

Procurement contact for PO: procurement@nimbusretail.com (they are standing by). Target timeline: PO in 10 business days assuming terms look reasonable.

Claire
